benchmark: LBMA Gold Price / COMEX GC front-month (GCQ26)
thesis_summary: Gold has corrected 25% from its January 2026 all-time high of $5,597, tracking almost exactly the rise in 10-year real yields to +2.25%. The near-term setup — death cross, elevated CFTC net longs at 181K contracts, fading ETF flows with a 298-tonne underwater overhang — does not support adding exposure; but the structural central-bank bid (~244 t in Q1 2026), long-run supply-demand near-balance, and a binary macro catalyst chain through September FOMC (dot plot) are sufficient reasons to hold rather than exit.
key_risks: ETF investor reversal at scale — the channel swung 804 t in a single year (FY2024→FY2025); even a 5% net redemption of 4,086 t ETF holdings equals ~200 t of fast, non-mine supply
Real yield re-acceleration above 2.3–2.4% if June CPI or July NFP disappoint the disinflation narrative
Simultaneous speculative long liquidation from the crowded 181K CFTC position + ETF redemptions from the 298 t estimated underwater overhang — an asymmetric downside squeeze
Fed reaffirms hike bias at July 29 FOMC, removing the rate-cut option that the June NFP miss reopened

key_levels.fair_value_range: 3860–4500 (rate-path conditional; upper end requires real yield durably at or below +1.5%)

relative_view: Most macro-conditional commodity in the tracked universe; gold is waiting for the Fed dot plot while copper, wheat, corn, soybeans, and cocoa sit on physical-balance and weather-driven theses that are independent of the real-yield environment — those offer more fundamentals-driven conviction windows right now
